audioDescription: Silent preview: no music, voice or sound effects.
limitations: Illustrative procedural scene inspired by New Kingdom register painting (the kicker credits the Nebamun paintings as the style inspiration); the figures are original drawings and are not archaeologically authentic copies or reconstructions.

Field refresh: palette.background_policy is scene_dependent, so the earlier warm #EEE3BB swatch is replaced by a cool gypsum/limestone ground (#E3E6DE). This is an authored choice, loosely after the grey grounds of some Old Kingdom tomb paintings. BACKGROUND_REVIEW.json lists 0 matched sources and no contact sheets, so no source-frame evidence was applied.
No preview recipe is demonstrated, because STYLE.json tech.preview_recipes is empty or null.
The plaster surface is approximated by a static fixed-seed SVG feTurbulence grain (cool grey mottle plus fine dark speckle); there is no real pigment, plaster relief or lighting simulation.

Mineral pigments are flat token fills (red #A84532, ochre #B9793C, blue #426C88, green #738261) with #3B2D23 contours; linen garments, eye whites and the light frieze stripe use an authored light linen tone (#F3F2EC).
The inscription column is intentionally an empty frame because no verified hieroglyphic text was supplied.
The procession uses x-only measured steps with fixed stride legs and shoulder/elbow pivot gestures; there is no gait cycle, perspective or shadow, by design.
Text contrast is checked at load with chroma.js against the flat field (#3B2D23 about 10.5:1; red headline about 4.7:1, which is large 54px text), not against the grain-composited pixels.
Tools are restricted to SVG, HTML/CSS, GSAP and DrawSVGPlugin, all checked as local and installed. No Blender or 3D tooling is used.
Authored at 1280x720 per the composition contract instead of the 1920x1080 named in the style implementation note.
